scope: Independent source review and every current skill/step, including setup, teaching, criterion, easier option, dependencies and claim scope. Exact sequences are editorial adaptations, not clinically validated protocols.
limitations: This is a documented evidence-informed editorial review, not an independent veterinary specialist endorsement or a validation trial of the app.
Sources disagree and differ in quality; agreement with all published dog-training literature is neither possible nor a sound standard.
Abstract-only and selected-section access are recorded in the source verification; not every entire paper was read.
The app supports individual adjustments, not diagnosis, medication decisions or guarantees of behavior without supervision.

NAME.title: Name recognition
NAME.decision: Attention to a name is taught before distraction; a name is not assumed to be a recall or evidence of emotional comfort.

NAME-1.title: Make the name predict a reward
NAME-1.reason: Name-reward pairing precedes the offered head turn; neither requires a sit or eye contact.

NAME-2.title: Reward the head turn
NAME-2.reason: Name-reward pairing precedes the offered head turn; neither requires a sit or eye contact.

MARK.title: Reward marker
MARK.decision: Pair the chosen gentle signal with prompt reward; markers are optional and no later action is required after a terminal marker.

MARK-1.title: Pair the signal with food
MARK-1.reason: A marker can be paired directly with reward and must not become a universal training gate.

TOUCH.title: Hand target
TOUCH.decision: Voluntary empty-hand nose targeting transfers only after the basic contact; do not push a hand into the face.

TOUCH-1.title: Capture a nose touch
TOUCH-1.reason: Voluntary palm contact precedes naming and small placement changes.

TOUCH-2.title: Add the cue and a little movement
TOUCH-2.reason: Voluntary palm contact precedes naming and small placement changes.

SIT.title: Sit
SIT.decision: Comfortable voluntary sitting and early lure fading are appropriate; sitting is not mandatory for safety or proof of calm.

SIT-1.title: Find a comfortable sit
SIT-1.reason: Comfortable sit acquisition precedes fading food and adding the cue; down and stand are independent.

SIT-2.title: Fade food in the guiding hand
SIT-2.reason: Comfortable sit acquisition precedes fading food and adding the cue; down and stand are independent.

DOWN.title: Lie down
DOWN.decision: Reward comfortable voluntary lowering without restraint; posture is distinct from relaxation.

DOWN-1.title: Guide or capture the down
DOWN-1.reason: Unforced down acquisition precedes cue transfer; a completed sit is unnecessary.

DOWN-2.title: Put down on a cue
DOWN-2.reason: Unforced down acquisition precedes cue transfer; a completed sit is unnecessary.

STAND.title: Stand
STAND.decision: A comfortable stationary stand is useful independently of a down; avoid repeatedly luring the dog to walk forward.

STAND-1.title: Follow into standing
STAND-1.reason: The dog may already offer a comfortable sit or rise naturally; a recorded sit grade is unnecessary.

FREE.title: Release from a position
FREE.decision: A release can be taught from any comfortable position; a completed sit is an unnecessary prerequisite.

FREE-1.title: Give the release meaning
FREE-1.reason: Release can be paired from any offered comfortable position, then separated from in-position rewards.

FREE-2.title: Separate reward from release
FREE-2.reason: Release can be paired from any offered comfortable position, then separated from in-position rewards.

DROP.title: Drop an item
DROP.decision: Trade willingly without chasing or prying; prevention and guarding assessment are distinct from a generic exchange exercise.

DROP-1.title: Make releasing worthwhile
DROP-1.reason: Easy voluntary trades precede cue-before-reward release, with no retrieve requirement.

DROP-2.title: Put the word before the trade
DROP-2.reason: Easy voluntary trades precede cue-before-reward release, with no retrieve requirement.

LEAVE.title: Leave an item alone
LEAVE.decision: Retain the cue, separately reinforce offered disengagement, teach modest context transfer, and keep hazards inaccessible without supervision.

LEAVE-1.title: Reward turning away
LEAVE-1.reason: Keep the first offered disengagement easy; prevent frustration and avoid implying that staring must continue until a cue.

LEAVE-2.title: Name the familiar turn away
LEAVE-2.reason: A cue can be useful without claiming unsupervised protection. The old title contradicted the protected setup.

LEAVE-3.title: Reward offered choices in another easy setup
LEAVE-3.reason: New context transfer needs its own record; it is not implied by learning the spoken cue.

LEAVE-4.title: Try a little distance while you stay present
LEAVE-4.reason: Handler-distance transfer is new learning. No absent-handler or household-wide safety claim is made.

WAIT.title: Short wait at an indoor doorway
WAIT.decision: A short safe interior-door pause can be offered or cued; release and physical exit security remain explicit.

WAIT-1.title: Reward a pause beside the doorway
WAIT-1.reason: Offered doorway pauses are compatible with a release cue; reinforcement can include access through a safe interior doorway.

WAIT-2.title: Add gentle door movement
WAIT-2.reason: Door movement, waiting time and context are separate difficulty dimensions.

TOILET.title: Toilet routine
TOILET.decision: Supervision, frequent individual opportunities and rewarding location are appropriate; medical changes are not disobedience.

TOILET-1.title: Reward the right location
TOILET-1.reason: Access routines precede cue pairing. Toilet access must never depend on obedience.

TOILET-2.title: Add a cue and an easy request
TOILET-2.reason: Access routines precede cue pairing. Toilet access must never depend on obedience.

RECALL.title: Come when called, first at home
RECALL.decision: Teach a distinct inviting approach directly, then transfer gradually; do not assume reliability around hazards or punish arrival.

RECALL-1.title: Build a short return
RECALL-1.reason: A distinct recall cue can be paired directly with approach; responding to the dog’s name is independent.

RECALL-2.title: Make arrival comfortable and worthwhile
RECALL-2.reason: Recall words directly predict approach; a name response is helpful but not required.

OTARGET.title: Nose target an object
OTARGET.decision: Teach broad stationary nose contact before placement or motion; this is a reusable contact action, not emotional treatment.

OTARGET-1.title: Discover the target
OTARGET-1.reason: Direct nose contact is acquired before the object-target cue and placement changes.

OTARGET-2.title: Add a cue and vary placement
OTARGET-2.reason: Direct nose contact is acquired before the object-target cue and placement changes.

STAY.title: Stay until released
STAY.decision: Increase short duration, distance and distraction separately; release and comfort matter more than a posture quota.

STAY-1.title: Stay through a small pause
STAY-1.reason: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

STAY-2.title: One small step away
STAY-2.reason: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

STAY-3.title: A modest everyday version
STAY-3.reason: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

STOP.title: Stop and stand on cue
STOP.decision: Reward a modest stationary pause in protected settings; this does not authorize traffic or off-leash safety tests.

STOP-1.title: Name a nearby stop
STOP-1.reason: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

STOP-2.title: Fade your own stopping prompt
STOP-2.reason: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

STOP-3.title: A little distance, still easy
STOP-3.reason: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

FRONT.title: Come to a front position
FRONT.decision: A comfortable arrival position is optional and distinct from a safety recall; do not crowd or physically align the dog.

FRONT-1.title: Find the space in front
FRONT-1.reason: A broad comfortable approach directly teaches the front position; no completed recall or sit is necessary.

FRONT-2.title: Name the front finish
FRONT-2.reason: A broad comfortable approach directly teaches the front position; no completed recall or sit is necessary.

FOODWAIT.title: Wait for a food-bowl invitation
FOODWAIT.decision: Keep bowl placement very brief and optional; never make meals conditional, repeatedly remove bowls, or treat guarding through compliance.

FOODWAIT-1.title: A tiny pause before placement
FOODWAIT-1.reason: Bowl manners are optional; essential nutrition and guarding treatment must not depend on compliance.

FOODWAIT-2.title: Lower once, then invite
FOODWAIT-2.reason: A momentary pause is paired directly with bowl access; meals and urgent access never depend on a grade.

MAT.title: Go to a mat
MAT.decision: Teach voluntary stationing and release separately from relaxed rest; a mat is not an enforced place to endure fear.

MAT-1.title: Make the mat worth approaching
MAT-1.reason: Approach and full-foot arrival precede adding the mat cue; settling and staying are separate behaviors.

MAT-2.title: Add the mat cue
MAT-2.reason: Approach and full-foot arrival precede adding the mat cue; settling and staying are separate behaviors.

SETTLE.title: Relax voluntarily on the mat
SETTLE.decision: Capture comfortable rest independently of cued stationing; a down, food-taking or immobility alone does not establish relaxation.

SETTLE-1.title: Capture comfortable resting
SETTLE-1.reason: Voluntary rest on a comfortable mat can be captured without a trained go-to-mat cue.

SETTLE-2.title: Stretch a restful interval
SETTLE-2.reason: Voluntary rest is captured directly; go-to-mat is an optional aid rather than a gate.

SETTLE-3.title: Pair an optional settle word
SETTLE-3.reason: Voluntary rest is captured directly; go-to-mat is an optional aid rather than a gate.

SAFE.title: Choose a safe resting area
SAFE.decision: A refuge requires actual comfort, escape management and trusted support; confinement or isolation is not automatically soothing.

SAFE-1.title: Build a pleasant refuge
SAFE-1.reason: Refuge exploration precedes attended management rehearsals. There is no requirement to be left alone.

SAFE-2.title: Practice brief separation from activity
SAFE-2.reason: Refuge exploration precedes attended management rehearsals. There is no requirement to be left alone.

ALONE.title: Very brief comfortable alone time
ALONE.decision: Camera-guided below-distress movement, tiny absences and departure-action comfort are distinct components; no crying-out or duration guarantee.

ALONE-1.title: Find an easy starting movement
ALONE-1.reason: Comfortable tiny within-room movements precede tiny absences and departure-action combinations.

ALONE-2.title: Try a moment out of view
ALONE-2.reason: Comfortable tiny within-room movements precede tiny absences and departure-action combinations.

ALONE-3.title: Make one departure action comfortable
ALONE-3.reason: Departure actions can be conditioned independently; they must not be gated behind out-of-view absences or treated as proof of absence tolerance.

RESTHEAD.title: Rest the head on a cushion
RESTHEAD.decision: Voluntary cushion contact can be taught directly; do not press the head down or infer calm solely from the trained posture.

RESTHEAD-1.title: Discover the cushion target
RESTHEAD-1.reason: This step teaches cushion contact directly; a hand chin rest is only an optional prompt.

RESTHEAD-2.title: Name a brief rest
RESTHEAD-2.reason: Cushion contact is shaped directly; a hand chin rest is an optional prompt rather than a prerequisite.

CRATE.title: Rest comfortably in a closed crate
CRATE.decision: Introduce an optional crate with voluntary entry and gradual comfortable closure; it is unsuitable as compulsory panic management.

CRATE-1.title: Choose to enter and exit
CRATE-1.reason: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

CRATE-2.title: Door movement with an open exit
CRATE-2.reason: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

CRATE-3.title: A momentary attended closure
CRATE-3.reason: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

VACATE.title: Get off furniture on cue
VACATE.decision: Reward moving to an inviting alternative without crowding, intimidation or grabbing; existing guarding requires an individual plan.

VACATE-1.title: Make leaving worthwhile
VACATE-1.reason: A voluntary route to a safe low landing precedes cue transfer; no pressure or high jump.

VACATE-2.title: Off before the invitation
VACATE-2.reason: A voluntary route to a safe low landing precedes cue transfer; no pressure or high jump.

ALLDONE.title: Finish an activity and move on
ALLDONE.decision: Pair a predictable end signal with a comfortable transition; it is not punishment or enforced loss of needed interaction.

ALLDONE-1.title: Predict a pleasant ending
ALLDONE-1.reason: A predictable pleasant transition acquires the end cue directly before transfer to another activity.

ALLDONE-2.title: Use the same ending elsewhere
ALLDONE-2.reason: A predictable pleasant transition acquires the end cue directly before transfer to another activity.

CHECK.title: Voluntary check-in
CHECK.decision: Reinforce offered check-ins and gradual transfer; do not demand prolonged eye contact or make food pairing contingent on it.

CHECK-1.title: Catch offered attention
CHECK-1.reason: Offered orientation is rewarded directly before incorporating ordinary walking.

CHECK-2.title: Reward while moving
CHECK-2.reason: Offered orientation is rewarded directly before incorporating ordinary walking.

LOOSE.title: Loose-leash walking
LOOSE.decision: Teach slack-lead walking on comfortable equipment in small increments; equipment fit is a safety check rather than an obedience grade.

LOOSE-1.title: Reward the starting zone
LOOSE-1.reason: Comfortable secure equipment is checked directly; recording a harness lesson is not a necessary learned component.

LOOSE-2.title: Add a few steps
LOOSE-2.reason: Slack-leash movement is taught directly; secure comfortable equipment is checked in the setup, without requiring a harness grade.

LOOSE-3.title: Use permission to sniff as a reward
LOOSE-3.reason: Slack-leash movement is taught directly; secure comfortable equipment is checked in the setup, without requiring a harness grade.

TURN.title: Happy turn-away
TURN.decision: Rehearse an inviting turn before mild distraction, without leash corrections; a retreat remains valid regardless of cue response.

TURN-1.title: Teach the turn without a trigger
TURN-1.reason: A trigger-free turn cue precedes travel and easy sniff interruptions; equipment comfort is a setup condition.

TURN-2.title: Add the leash and an exit destination
TURN-2.reason: The learned turn is necessary; suitable comfortable equipment is a direct setup check rather than a mandatory harness grade.

TURN-3.title: Rehearse a gentle planned interruption
TURN-3.reason: A trigger-free turn cue precedes travel and easy sniff interruptions; equipment comfort is a setup condition.

FIND.title: Find food on the ground
FIND.decision: Invited food search on known safe ground is compatible with leave-it training; avoid competition, ingestion hazards or overwhelming triggers.

FIND-1.title: Pair the cue with a visible scatter
FIND-1.reason: A visible food scatter acquires its own cue before the ground surface changes.

FIND-2.title: Move the search to an easy outdoor spot
FIND-2.reason: A visible food scatter acquires its own cue before the ground surface changes.

SIDE.title: Move behind you or to the far side
SIDE.decision: Reward a comfortable side position without physical placement; this optional alignment does not replace free movement and sniffing.

SIDE-1.title: Guide the side change
SIDE-1.reason: The hand target actually guides the broad route; the far-side cue follows this action.

SIDE-2.title: Add a cue and short movement
SIDE-2.reason: The hand target actually guides the broad route; the far-side cue follows this action.

HEEL.title: Heel on cue
HEEL.decision: Short precise positioning is optional, with early lure fading and releases; it is not the standard for an entire ordinary walk.

HEEL-1.title: Find the heel position
HEEL-1.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

HEEL-2.title: Heel means come beside me
HEEL-2.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

HEEL-3.title: Maintain position while moving
HEEL-3.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

HEEL-4.title: Turns, stops and a clear release
HEEL-4.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

RHYTHM.title: Counted walking rhythm
RHYTHM.decision: Predictable short walking patterns can help communication; no claim that a pattern cures fear or overrides the need for distance.

RHYTHM-1.title: Make the count predictable
RHYTHM-1.reason: Predictable stationary count-reward pairings precede a few optional walking cycles; exact heel position and trigger exposure are not part of this game.

RHYTHM-2.title: Walk a few counted steps
RHYTHM-2.reason: Predictable stationary count-reward pairings precede a few optional walking cycles; exact heel position and trigger exposure are not part of this game.

CURB.title: Pause at a curb
CURB.decision: Start at harmless flat lines, then a protected real curb with human traffic decisions; no automatic road-safety claim.

CURB-1.title: Stop at a pretend edge
CURB-1.reason: A harmless floor line teaches the pause before quiet real-edge transfer; no claim that dogs judge traffic.

CURB-2.title: Transfer to a quiet real edge
CURB-2.reason: A harmless floor line teaches the pause before quiet real-edge transfer; no claim that dogs judge traffic.

CROSS.title: Cross a quiet road together
CROSS.decision: Indoor rehearsal follows flat-line preparation; the actual curb prerequisite moves to the real crossing, where humans decide safety.

CROSS-1.title: Rehearse the whole path indoors
CROSS-1.reason: Indoor route rehearsal needs the flat-line pause, not completed exposure at a real curb.

CROSS-2.title: One quiet checked crossing
CROSS-2.reason: Real crossing adds the actual curb context only when that context is introduced.

SLOW.title: Match a slower walking pace
SLOW.decision: Reward modest changes to walking pace without force; exercise and pace must suit individual health and normal movement.

SLOW-1.title: Notice a pace change
SLOW-1.reason: Known slack-leash steps support a small pace change, then a few slower steps.

SLOW-2.title: Several unhurried steps
SLOW-2.reason: Known slack-leash steps support a small pace change, then a few slower steps.

WALKPAUSE.title: Pause while the handler stops
WALKPAUSE.decision: Practice brief comfortable pauses and release rather than prolonged suppression of exploration or distress.

WALKPAUSE-1.title: A one-second walking pause
WALKPAUSE-1.reason: A direct short pause beside a stopped human precedes a brief ordinary hand movement; formal heel is unnecessary.

WALKPAUSE-2.title: A brief practical interruption
WALKPAUSE-2.reason: A direct short pause beside a stopped human precedes a brief ordinary hand movement; formal heel is unnecessary.

DOG.title: Seeing a dog predicts good things
DOG.decision: Brief supported sightings and prompt trigger-food pairing begin at a comfortable distance; no obedience or threshold testing is required.

DOG-1.title: Find a comfortable viewing setup
DOG-1.reason: Assessment should not withhold support until a later lesson.

DOG-2.title: Pair the sight with food
DOG-2.reason: An individually comfortable sighting precedes positive pairings, then small controlled movement changes.

DOG-3.title: Vary one easy feature
DOG-3.reason: An individually comfortable sighting precedes positive pairings, then small controlled movement changes.

DISENGAGE.title: Choose to look away from another dog
DISENGAGE.decision: Teach an offered attention shift at an easy distance, distinct from counterconditioning; never wait through escalating fixation.

DISENGAGE-1.title: Reward a brief offered turn-away
DISENGAGE-1.reason: Easy sight-food pairing supports comfortable observation before rewarding offered look-aways; no required stare or obedience pose.

DISENGAGE-2.title: Practice a choice and retreat
DISENGAGE-2.reason: Easy sight-food pairing supports comfortable observation before rewarding offered look-aways; no required stare or obedience pose.

PARALLEL.title: Walk parallel at a comfortable distance
PARALLEL.decision: Both dogs need comfortable wide movement and retreat; trigger-food support need not wait for a check-in or eventual greeting.

PARALLEL-1.title: Add parallel movement
PARALLEL-1.reason: Maintain trigger-food pairing during comfortable movement; check-ins are separately reinforced rather than a condition of support.

PARALLEL-2.title: Extend the easy stretch
PARALLEL-2.reason: Comfort with a moving helper dog and a rehearsed turn support controlled walking and safe exits.

PASS.title: Make a wide planned pass
PASS.decision: The first stationary-helper pass needs dog comfort and a turn; moving-helper competence is introduced only for a moving pass.

PASS-1.title: Rehearse a staged pass
PASS-1.reason: The first pass uses a stationary comfortable helper and a rehearsed exit; completed parallel moving-dog walks and sniff interruptions are unnecessary gates.

PASS-2.title: Try a gentle opposite-direction pass
PASS-2.reason: The moving-helper pass now explicitly needs comfortable dog movement at the step that introduces it.

STRANGER.title: Feel safer with an unfamiliar adult
STRANGER.decision: Use a distant neutral adult with optional retreat, no food lure toward touch and no obligatory greeting.

STRANGER-1.title: Start with an uninteresting person
STRANGER-1.reason: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

STRANGER-2.title: Make one small movement predictable
STRANGER-2.reason: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

STRANGER-3.title: Practice with a second adult separately
STRANGER-3.reason: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

KNOCK.title: Feel comfortable hearing a knock
KNOCK.decision: Separate a faint controllable tap from mat behavior and the real arrival chain; do not repeat overwhelming knocks waiting for quiet.

KNOCK-1.title: Pair a very soft tap
KNOCK-1.reason: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

KNOCK-2.title: Transfer to the actual door
KNOCK-2.reason: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

KNOCK-3.title: Change one part of the knock
KNOCK-3.reason: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

BELL.title: Feel comfortable hearing the doorbell
BELL.decision: Faint recording and physical bell are separate contexts; pair the noticed sound without requiring silence or a station first.

BELL-1.title: Start with a faint recording
BELL-1.reason: A faint recording precedes a controllable real bell. An unmodifiable frightening bell needs management, not forced advancement.

BELL-2.title: Transfer carefully to the actual bell
BELL-2.reason: A faint recording precedes a controllable real bell. An unmodifiable frightening bell needs management, not forced advancement.

DOOR.title: Knock means go to the mat
DOOR.decision: Combine fluent arrival components under controlled rehearsal; an entry-management plan remains necessary for unplanned arrivals.

DOOR-1.title: Link the two familiar events
DOOR-1.reason: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

DOOR-2.title: Let the knock become the cue
DOOR-2.reason: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

DOOR-3.title: Add your own doorway movement
DOOR-3.reason: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

VISITOR.title: Comfortable separated visitor routine
VISITOR.decision: A fully separated comfortable visit is a valid endpoint; optional distant viewing must not block nonvisual visitor-action practice.

VISITOR-1.title: Rehearse without a visitor
VISITOR-1.reason: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

VISITOR-2.title: Bring in one quiet adult while separated
VISITOR-2.reason: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

VISITOR-3.title: Offer an optional distant view
VISITOR-3.reason: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

VISITOR-4.title: Add one visitor action
VISITOR-4.reason: An optional view must not become a gate for nonvisual visitor practice.

GREET.title: Four paws greeting with familiar people
GREET.decision: Greeting is voluntary and unnecessary for successful coexistence; approach for food is not permission to touch.

GREET-1.title: Reward four paws before approach
GREET-1.reason: Four-paw comfort during an easy approach precedes optional voluntary contact; sitting is not required.

GREET-2.title: Offer a brief optional hello
GREET-2.reason: Four-paw comfort during an easy approach precedes optional voluntary contact; sitting is not required.

HANDOFF.title: Change leash handlers comfortably
HANDOFF.decision: Use a familiar consenting helper and reversible small changes; transferred equipment does not justify restraint or separation distress.

HANDOFF-1.title: Walk beside the helper
HANDOFF-1.reason: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

HANDOFF-2.title: A still, secure transfer
HANDOFF-2.reason: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

HANDOFF-3.title: A short walk with the new handler
HANDOFF-3.reason: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

SOUND.title: Controlled sound practice
SOUND.decision: Controlled brief sound-food pairing changes one dimension at a time; replace historical no-comfort guidance and avoid recording-to-real-event guarantees.

SOUND-1.title: Find a faint noticeable version
SOUND-1.reason: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

SOUND-2.title: Change one sound feature
SOUND-2.reason: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

SOUND-3.title: Try a modest realistic variation
SOUND-3.reason: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

OUTSIDE.title: Noises outside and window activity
OUTSIDE.decision: Different mild outdoor sights and sounds need separately controlled starts; visual and auditory presentations are not interchangeable certification.

OUTSIDE-1.title: Reduce constant exposure
OUTSIDE-1.reason: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

OUTSIDE-2.title: Pair one manageable outside event
OUTSIDE-2.reason: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

OUTSIDE-3.title: Practice returning away from the window
OUTSIDE-3.reason: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

STORM.title: Prepare for unavoidable noise events
STORM.decision: Rehearse protection and support before real events; plan readiness can be recorded without inducing noise or claiming fear is cured.

STORM-1.title: Rehearse the support arrangement
STORM-1.reason: Support and management must be accessible immediately; this step rehearses the refuge itself without requiring an earlier grade.

STORM-2.title: Prepare to use and review the plan
STORM-2.reason: A support plan can be ready before an unavoidable event occurs. Completion must not require manufactured exposure or imply a cure.

OBJECT.title: Comfort with an object or appliance
OBJECT.decision: Still sight, motion and sound can be conditioned separately; food does not require exploration, and combinations await comfortable components.

OBJECT-1.title: Start with the object still and off
OBJECT-1.reason: Counterconditioning does not require approach, calm exploration or obedience before food.

OBJECT-2.title: Add a tiny movement
OBJECT-2.reason: Comfortable sight precedes small object movement, then separately introduced appliance sound.

OBJECT-3.title: Introduce sound separately
OBJECT-3.reason: Sound conditioning can begin independently of visible movement; combinations require both components to be comfortable.

MOTION.title: Bikes, moving vehicles, or joggers at a distance
MOTION.decision: Start well away from traffic or controlled moving helpers with retreat; use physical security and avoid motion-based flooding.

MOTION-1.title: Watch a slow distant version
MOTION-1.reason: Comfortable distant slow movement precedes a tiny speed or duration change; no approach or chase.

MOTION-2.title: Change speed or duration separately
MOTION-2.reason: Comfortable distant slow movement precedes a tiny speed or duration change; no approach or chase.

CAR.title: Comfort around a parked car
CAR.decision: Stationary-car comfort precedes travel; use appropriate transport restraint and veterinary assessment of motion sickness or severe distress.

CAR-1.title: Begin near the stationary car
CAR-1.reason: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

CAR-2.title: Teach entry and immediate exit
CAR-2.reason: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

CAR-3.title: Add restraint and door movement separately
CAR-3.reason: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

ELEVATOR.title: Ride a quiet elevator comfortably
ELEVATOR.decision: Introduce empty-car sounds, voluntary entry and a short ride separately; keep dog and handler together with no leash through closing doors.

ELEVATOR-1.title: Watch from a comfortable distance
ELEVATOR-1.reason: Door-cycle observation precedes stationary voluntary entry before a tiny attended ride.

ELEVATOR-2.title: Enter and exit while stationary
ELEVATOR-2.reason: Prevent a line crossing a closing elevator door; enter and exit together with ordinary short equipment.

ELEVATOR-3.title: One short quiet ride
ELEVATOR-3.reason: Door-cycle observation precedes stationary voluntary entry before a tiny attended ride.

AUTODOOR.title: Pass through automatic doors
AUTODOOR.decision: Observe safely before a controlled broad passage; never rely on a sensor detecting a dog or put the dog in the opening to activate it.

AUTODOOR-1.title: Watch the moving panels
AUTODOOR-1.reason: Comfortable panel observation precedes a fully human-checked wide passage; a trained hoop pass is unrelated.

AUTODOOR-2.title: One generous walking pass
AUTODOOR-2.reason: Keep handler and dog together, and ordinary leash clear of automatic doors.

HARNESS.title: Comfortable harness routine
HARNESS.decision: Voluntary approach, head passage and comfortable fitting are separate; fit, movement and withdrawal matter more than a completed grade.

HARNESS-1.title: Make equipment appearance pleasant
HARNESS-1.reason: Appearance and buckle comfort precede voluntary placement, then fastening and a few steps.

HARNESS-2.title: Invite voluntary fitting

HANDLE-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

COLLAR-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

RINSE-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

RINSE-3.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

EAR-1.title: Hand movement toward the ear
EAR-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

EAR-2.title: A momentary outer-flap view
EAR-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

SIDELIE.title: Lie comfortably on one side

SIDELIE-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

SIDELIE-3.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

RAMP.title: Walk a low stable ramp
RAMP.decision: Begin flat and stable, then very low with traction; no jumping, elevation prescription or assumed suitability for pain or injury.

RAMP-1.reason: A flat secured pass precedes a tiny supported slope; a scale or raised-platform grade is unrelated.

RAMP-2.title: A tiny supported slope
RAMP-2.reason: A flat secured pass precedes a tiny supported slope; a scale or raised-platform grade is unrelated.

SCRATCH.title: Scratch a designated board
SCRATCH.decision: A secured safe scratch surface can be enrichment; nail health and tool suitability need individual assessment, not forced paw placement.

SCRATCH-1.title: Find one paw movement
SCRATCH-1.reason: Direct foot movement on a stable board precedes naming one tiny scrape; nail contact and clipping are separate.

SCRATCH-2.title: Name one gentle scrape
SCRATCH-2.reason: Direct foot movement on a stable board precedes naming one tiny scrape; nail contact and clipping are separate.

BREAKBUTTON.title: Press to request a break
BREAKBUTTON.decision: Give a simple trained break signal an actual pause; a button press is not required before respecting avoidance or withdrawal.

BREAKBUTTON-1.title: A press always opens a break
BREAKBUTTON-1.reason: A known button press is immediately honored as a break before offered requests; ordinary withdrawal always remains valid.

BREAKBUTTON-2.title: Wait for a voluntary request
BREAKBUTTON-2.reason: A known button press is immediately honored as a break before offered requests; ordinary withdrawal always remains valid.

TAKE.title: Take a safe object
TAKE.decision: Shape voluntary gentle pickup and reward each marker promptly; reset only after willing release or trade, without mouth insertion.

TAKE-1.title: Shape gentle mouth contact
TAKE-1.reason: Reinforce one small criterion at a time and reset only after voluntary release or trade; avoid taking objects forcibly.

TAKE-2.title: Add take before the offer
TAKE-2.reason: A grip marker earns prompt reward; release to eat is accepted without an additional obedience demand.

HOLD.title: Hold gently
HOLD.decision: Build momentary gentle supported grip before carrying; accept release to eat and never close the jaw or add neck resistance.

HOLD-1.title: Build a supported brief hold
HOLD-1.reason: Known take and release support safe brief holds, then unsupported weight and slightly longer duration.

HOLD-2.title: Remove your support briefly
HOLD-2.reason: Known take and release support safe brief holds, then unsupported weight and slightly longer duration.

GIVE.title: Deliver into your hand
GIVE.decision: A gentle hand delivery uses known object handling, without prying; receiving the item is separately reinforced before travel.

GIVE-1.title: Place the receiving hand under the object
GIVE-1.reason: A short comfortable hold and release are actual components of hand delivery, which is then named separately.

GIVE-2.title: Fade the extra drop cue
GIVE-2.reason: A short comfortable hold and release are actual components of hand delivery, which is then named separately.

CARRY.title: Carry a few steps
CARRY.decision: Add very short transport after a comfortable grip and delivery; mark the completed action rather than ending a carry prematurely.

CARRY-1.title: Add one step toward you
CARRY-1.reason: Comfortable unsupported hold and hand delivery precede a few inches of travel, then a few steps.

CARRY-2.title: Build a short carry
CARRY-2.reason: Comfortable unsupported hold and hand delivery precede a few inches of travel, then a few steps.

FETCH.title: Retrieve a placed toy
FETCH.decision: Stationary pickup needs hand delivery; outward travel adds carrying at the step that uses it, with safe reachable props.

FETCH-1.title: Lower pickup toward the floor
FETCH-1.reason: A stationary pickup from a lower surface uses known take/hold/give, covered by hand delivery; traveling carries are not used until the next step.

FETCH-2.title: Add a little outward travel
FETCH-2.reason: The short outward retrieve now explicitly requires carrying at the step that introduces travel.

BOX.title: Put toys in a basket
BOX.decision: Basket release can start from hand delivery; floor collection adds the retrieve only where it is needed.

BOX-1.title: Drop over a nearby basket
BOX-1.reason: Hand delivery transfers to a basket release independently; adding floor pickup and travel explicitly requires retrieve.

BOX-2.title: Add a small carry to the basket
BOX-2.reason: Hand delivery transfers to a basket release independently; adding floor pickup and travel explicitly requires retrieve.

SEARCH.title: Easy food search
SEARCH.decision: Simple safe visible food placements precede mild concealment; this is enjoyable exploration, not a clinical anxiety intervention.

SEARCH-1.title: Make the first hides obvious
SEARCH-1.reason: Visible food investigation precedes tiny partly hidden searches; no wait or target is necessary.

SEARCH-2.title: Hide just one easy piece
SEARCH-2.reason: Visible food investigation precedes tiny partly hidden searches; no wait or target is necessary.

TUG.title: Gentle tug with a release
TUG.decision: Mutual low-force play and willing release are appropriate for dogs that enjoy them; avoid forced grip, high movement or guarding tests.

TUG-1.title: Invite a tiny low game
TUG-1.reason: A rewarded release is used to end gentle play safely, followed by the short game-ending routine.

TUG-2.title: Build a predictable finish
TUG-2.reason: A rewarded release is used to end gentle play safely, followed by the short game-ending routine.

SPIN.title: Small comfortable spin
SPIN.decision: Use a broad comfortable floor turn and fade lures; skip repetitive or tight turns for dogs with discomfort.

SPIN-1.title: Guide a partial circle
SPIN-1.reason: A comfortable broad turn precedes fading the lure; reverse direction is optional and separate.

SPIN-2.title: Fade the lure and add the word
SPIN-2.reason: A comfortable broad turn precedes fading the lure; reverse direction is optional and separate.

PAW.title: Offer a paw
PAW.decision: A low voluntary offer does not authorize paw restraint for care; maintain balance, brief contact and prompt reward.

PAW-1.title: Capture a small paw lift
PAW-1.reason: A voluntary low paw offer precedes cue transfer; no restraint or forced limb placement.

PAW-2.title: Add the cue and a quick release
PAW-2.reason: A voluntary low paw offer precedes cue transfer; no restraint or forced limb placement.

PULL.title: Tug a rope handle
PULL.decision: Use an intact safe handle, negligible resistance and prompt reward after marking; do not add a release demand before the promised reward.

PULL-1.title: Take the rope handle
PULL-1.reason: A terminal marker promises prompt reward without an extra release command as a hidden requirement.

PULL-2.title: Reward tiny backward tension
PULL-2.reason: Do not mark the pull and then require another response before delivering the promised reward.

PULL-3.title: Transfer to a lightweight hinged prop
PULL-3.reason: Take and drop support gentle rope grip, tiny resistance and easy board movement; the refrigerator is a later independent transfer.

NAMECTX.title: Name response in new settings
NAMECTX.decision: Rebuild name response in specified easy new settings; a response in one context does not certify attention around fear or high distraction.

NAMECTX-1.title: Change rooms, keep everything easy
NAMECTX-1.reason: The original name turn transfers to another quiet room, outdoors and then a mild ordinary distraction.

NAMECTX-2.title: Try a quiet secure outdoor place
NAMECTX-2.reason: The original name turn transfers to another quiet room, outdoors and then a mild ordinary distraction.

NAMECTX-3.title: Add one mild controlled distraction
NAMECTX-3.reason: The original name turn transfers to another quiet room, outdoors and then a mild ordinary distraction.

RECALLCTX.title: Recall in a new safe setting
RECALLCTX.decision: Use enclosure or a safely managed line on suitable body equipment; increase context difficulty without reeling in or hard stops.

RECALLCTX-1.title: Restart short in a quiet outdoor area
RECALLCTX-1.reason: The indoor recall transfers; comfortable fitted long-line equipment is a safety condition, not an extra obedience prerequisite.

RECALLCTX-2.title: Change distance or mild interest separately
RECALLCTX-2.reason: A fluent indoor recall is the learned component; safe enclosure or comfortable line equipment is checked directly.

MATCTX.title: Mat comfort in another place
MATCTX.decision: Transfer stationing to a new room before adding quiet rest; the rest prerequisite belongs at the step that uses it.

MATCTX-1.title: Transfer the familiar mat
MATCTX-1.reason: Moving the mat cue to a new room precedes resting and need not wait for settled duration.

MATCTX-2.title: Rebuild a restful interval
MATCTX-2.reason: The quiet-rest component is required at the step that actually transfers it.

WALKCTX.title: Loose walking in another place
WALKCTX.decision: Transfer the learned slack-lead action in easier new settings; equipment and optional exits do not become unrelated grade gates.

WALKCTX-1.title: Restart with one or two steps
WALKCTX-1.reason: Transfer uses loose walking; a turn-away remains a useful optional exit, not part of the taught walking action.

WALKCTX-2.title: Add ordinary variation carefully
WALKCTX-2.reason: Loose walking transfers directly to an easy new setting; a turn-away remains an optional exit aid.

KEEP.title: Maintain skills and review changes
KEEP.decision: Refresh only observed exact criteria and contexts; absent logs do not establish forgetting, and changed fear calls for assessment rather than drilling.

KEEP-1.title: Plan short enjoyable refreshers
KEEP-1.reason: A refresher does not justify promoting every stage or broader context without observing its criterion.

KEEP-2.title: Review one trigger in comparable conditions
KEEP-2.reason: A maintenance routine precedes a supported review of comparable journal records; no all-catalog completion gate.

BOW.title: Take a little bow

NOSEBALL-3.reason: Ball contact precedes a gentle movable nudge, then a named short roll; generic object targeting is optional.

BOWL-2.reason: The known cued ball roll is transferred to one soft pin before a small cluster.

CROSSPAW-2.reason: Make the reward explicit and accept movement after marking rather than extending a strained pose.

SHAKEOFF.title: Shake off on cue

CIRCLEME-2.reason: The known hand target guides broad independent halves before joining the loop around a stationary person.

UNROLL-2.title: A short unrolling action
UNROLL-2.reason: Known object nose targeting transfers to a loose roll, then one or two gentle nudges; ball pushing is unnecessary.

LEFTRIGHT-3.title: Make a fair directional choice
LEFTRIGHT-3.reason: Each target-direction pairing uses known mat arrival independently; mixed choices require both, with fixed start orientation.

NOD.title: A small nose-target nod

NOD-2.title: Fade to a tiny nod signal
NOD-2.reason: Known object targeting guides two very close natural head heights before a small cue transfer.

POINT-2.reason: Known mat arrival transfers to a gesture with one target before two-target mixed choices; directional words are independent.

BACK-3.reason: A voluntary backward weight shift precedes one named step and then two or three; no body pressure.

CONE.title: Go around a cone

CONE-1.title: Follow a wide arc
CONE-1.reason: The known hand target actually guides a broad arc before naming and joining the loop.

CONE-2.title: Join and name the loop
CONE-2.reason: The known hand target actually guides a broad arc before naming and joining the loop.

CONEEIGHT.title: Figure eight around two markers

CONEEIGHT-1.reason: Known separate cone loops precede their broad connection; no leg weave is required.

CONEEIGHT-2.title: Connect the loops
CONEEIGHT-2.reason: Known separate cone loops precede their broad connection; no leg weave is required.

FEET.title: Front paws on a flat target

FEET-1.reason: Direct front-foot contact precedes two-front-foot targeting, then the cue, all at floor level.

FEET-2.title: Reward two front paws
FEET-2.reason: Direct front-foot contact precedes two-front-foot targeting, then the cue, all at floor level.

FEET-3.title: Add the floor-target cue
FEET-3.reason: Direct front-foot contact precedes two-front-foot targeting, then the cue, all at floor level.

HOOP.title: Walk through a floor-level hoop
HOOP.decision: Use a broad floor-level opening with optional guidance, not jumping; remove duplicate wording without changing the criterion.

HOOP-1.title: Explore the open shape
HOOP-1.reason: Exploring an opening and following a small optional lure can be taught directly; a finished hand target unnecessarily blocks exploration.

HOOP-2.title: Name the walking pass
HOOP-2.reason: Remove duplicated wording without changing the exercise.

TUNNEL.title: Explore an open tunnel
TUNNEL.decision: An open broad short floor-level passage is voluntary; never trap or push the dog through, and skip if confinement is uncomfortable.
